record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: QSOs defined by factorized heredity coefficients
record.original_question: Develop a theory for quadratic stochastic operators whose heredity coefficients factor as P_{ij,k} = a_{ik} b_{jk}, equivalently operators of the form (V(x))_k = (A(x))_k · (B(x))_k where A(x) and B(x) are linear maps determined by the matrices A = (a_{ik}) and B = (b_{jk}) subject to the stochasticity constraints. Study their structural and dynamical properties as a generalization of Volterra QSOs.

evidence.quote: Consider QSO (4), (5) with additional condition Pij,k = aik bjk , ∀i, j, k ∈ E ... Then the QSO V corresponding to the coefficients (20) has the form x′k = (V (x))k = (A(x))k · (B(x))k .
Problem 20. Develop theory of QSOs defined by (21).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E=\{1,2,\dots,m\}$ and let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m_{\ge 0}:\sum_{k=1}^m x_k=1\}$ be the standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on $S^{m-1}$ is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ defined by
$$
(V(x))_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\,x_i x_j,\qquad k\in E,
$$
where the heredity coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ satisfy
$$
P_{ij,k}\ge 0,\qquad P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k},\qquad \sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1\quad\text{for all }i,j,k\in E.
$$
Consider the subclass of QSOs whose heredity coefficients admit a factorization
$$
P_{ij,k} = a_{ik}\,b_{jk},\qquad i,j,k\in E,
$$
for some real matrices $A=(a_{ik})$ and $B=(b_{jk})$, where the constraints above force the symmetry $a_{ik}b_{jk}=a_{jk}b_{ik}$ together with the non-negativity and stochasticity conditions
$$
a_{ik}b_{jk}\ge 0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^m a_{ik}b_{jk}=1\quad\text{for all }i,j\in E.
$$
For such operators one has the Hadamard-product representation
$$
(V(x))_k = (A(x))_k\cdot (B(x))_k,\qquad\text{where }(A(x))_k=\sum_i a_{ik}x_i,\ (B(x))_k=\sum_j b_{jk}x_j.
$$
Develop a theory for this class of QSOs as a generalization of Volterra QSOs: characterize the admissible pairs $(A,B)$; describe fixed points, invariant subsets, and ergodic/non-ergodic behavior; analyze the long-term dynamics of the iterates $V^n(x)$ for $x\in S^{m-1}$; and identify the structural properties (e.g., conservativity, dissipativity, regularity) that distinguish this family from the general QSO class and from Volterra QSOs.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results show extensive literature on quadratic stochastic operators, including Volterra QSOs, F-QSOs, dissipative QSOs, and permutation-type QSOs, but no source explicitly labeled as developing the full theory of QSOs with factorized heredity coefficients $P_{ij,k}=a_{ik}b_{jk}$. The status of this program could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators and Their Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of QSO classes including Volterra and related families.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys of QSOs do not single out the factorized class as solved.

status_evidence.title: F-quadratic stochastic operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a related restricted class of QSOs.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations of Volterra QSOs have been pursued in different directions, but not specifically the multiplicative factorization form.
